summary: Baileys fork pulls libsignal from an unpinned personal GitHub repo at install time
details: package.json for @zanxiky/baileys@1.1.0 declares the `libsignal` dependency as `github:tenka-san/libsignal-node` — a non-registry git source on an unaffiliated personal GitHub account with no commit SHA and no integrity check. On `npm install`, npm clones the current default-branch tip of that repository and executes any lifecycle scripts it contains, so the owner of the `tenka-san` GitHub account controls arbitrary code execution on every installer's machine, and the referenced bytes can change at any time without any version bump to this package. The GitHub account is unrelated to the upstream Baileys publisher (whiskeysockets), and the fork itself appears to be a lookalike of the Baileys WhatsApp library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
